Quillan Bay National Bank (QBNB) is filing this report on Raymond J. Castellano (SSN ending 7781), a self-employed tile contractor doing business as Castellano Custom Tile, for suspected structuring of cash deposits to avoid currency transaction reporting.

From 02/07/2022 through 04/28/2022, Mr. Castellano made 16 cash deposits totaling $150,200.00: $103,400.00 into personal checking account ending 3910 and $46,800.00 into business checking account ending 2118 (DBA Castellano Custom Tile). Every deposit was between $8,800.00 and $9,850.00, just below the $10,000 currency transaction reporting threshold. Deposits were made at the Lodi, March Lane and Pacific Avenue branches. On 3 business days he deposited cash at two different branches on the same day (for example, 03/01/2022: $9,650.00 at the Lodi branch and $9,250.00 at the March Lane branch; 03/22/2022: $9,850.00 at the March Lane branch and $9,550.00 at the Pacific Avenue branch). Because those same-day deposits aggregated above $10,000, the bank filed CTRs for those dates. Tellers noted the cash was mostly $100 and $50 bills, some still in paper bank straps.

When the business account was opened in 2019, Mr. Castellano described Castellano Custom Tile as a residential tile installation business and estimated cash deposits of about $3,000 per month, with most customers paying by check or card. During this period cash deposits averaged $56,445.53 per month, while check and card deposits to the business account totaled $42,970.55 for the whole period. The volume and pattern of cash are inconsistent with the customer's stated business and expected activity.

The activity was identified by the bank's transaction monitoring system (alert QBN-22-03817) and reviewed by the BSA department. The bank is monitoring the accounts. Supporting documentation is retained by the institution and is available to law enforcement and regulators upon request.

Corrado Street Savings Bank is filing this report on Meridel Trading Partners LP (EIN ending 8842), an importer and wholesaler of home furnishings, for wire activity indicative of trade-based money laundering.

From 02/02/2023 through 04/21/2023, operating account ending 1878 received 11 incoming international wires totaling $727,883.77 from Al Noor General Trading FZE (Dubai, UAE), Cendana Commodities Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), Grand Lotus Trading Co., Ltd. (Hong Kong) and Pacific Orchid Holdings Ltd. (Hong Kong). None of these companies appears on the customer's list of U.S. retail and hospitality buyers provided at onboarding. Within one to three days of each credit, the partnership sent outgoing wires to Binh Duong Teak Furniture JSC (Vietnam) and Mekar Rattan Industries Sdn. Bhd. (Malaysia) totaling $613,383.92, leaving roughly 16% of inflows in the account.

At the bank's request the customer provided commercial invoices and bills of lading for three shipments. The invoices describe teak dining sets at unit prices about three times those on comparable shipments the bank has seen, and the declared container weights on the bills of lading are low for the stated quantities. Third-party payments from entities in jurisdictions unrelated to the goods, combined with apparent over-invoicing, are consistent with trade-based money laundering. The general partner is Anika S. Varga. Supporting documentation is retained by the institution and is available to law enforcement and regulators upon request.

Larkfield Commerce Bank is filing this report on Brightwater Bistro Group, Inc. (EIN ending 7153), which operates four full-service restaurants in the Phoenix area, for cash deposits split across branches and employees and a sharp shift from card to cash receipts.

From 03/01/2023 through 05/23/2023, operating account ending 1075 received 50 cash deposits totaling $382,920.00, each between $5,330.00 and $9,880.00, made at the Central Phoenix, Old Town Scottsdale, Tempe Marketplace and Mesa Riverview branches by four employees the bank identifies as restaurant managers (Dana Ruelas, Pete Arkwright, Simone Bell and Marco Treviño). Deposits were usually made at two or three branches on the same day. The bank aggregated them and filed CTRs for 23 business days on which the combined total exceeded $10,000.

Cash was 61% of the account's deposits in this period, compared with about 18% in 2022. Card-processor settlement deposits fell from an average of $186,400.00 to $92,300.00 per month while the number of locations stayed the same. The shift suggests card sales may be being routed elsewhere or that cash from another source is being commingled with restaurant receipts. Supporting documentation is retained by the institution and is available to law enforcement and regulators upon request.

Funds in the personal account were used for payments on a boat loan and transfers to a brokerage account. On 06/08/2025 the originating bank sent a recall request stating that the victim had been sent altered payment instructions from a spoofed email address. The bank froze the remaining $37,720.00 and returned it. Supporting documentation is retained by the institution and is available to law enforcement and regulators upon request.

Northvale Home Lending Corp. is filing this report on loan applicant Lorraine P. Whitcomb (SSN ending 3305) for suspected origination fraud involving falsified income documents.

On 09/14/2023, Ms. Whitcomb applied for a $640,000.00 purchase-money mortgage on a property in Scottsdale, Arizona. She submitted 2021 and 2022 Forms W-2 from Halcyon Logistics Group LLC showing wages of $198,750 and $212,400, a 2022 Form 1040 showing adjusted gross income of $231,060, and two months of bank statements. During verification on 09/26/2023, the employer phone number on the W-2s rang to Ms. Whitcomb's own mobile number, Halcyon Logistics Group LLC had no active registration with the Arizona Corporation Commission, and the bank statements did not match the format used by the issuing bank. The lender denied the application on 10/03/2023. No funds were disbursed. Supporting documentation is retained by the institution and is available to law enforcement and regulators upon request.
